items.plain: Don't take pride in wealth, powerful friends, strength, looks or skill; illness can take the body's gifts quickly, and every good gift comes from God, who wants to give even Himself.
items.core_idea: Boast only in God, the giver of every gift

items.plain: Don't think yourself better than others; God sees differently than people do. Assume others have more good than you. Putting yourself below everyone does no harm; the humble have peace, the proud have envy and anger.
items.core_idea: Humility brings peace; pride brings envy and anger

items.plain: We should love everyone but not be close with everyone. Someone admired from a distance may disappoint in person, and getting too familiar can make others see our faults and like us less.
items.core_idea: Love all, but keep close friendship for few

items.plain: People naturally favour those who agree with them, but with Christ among us we must sometimes give up our opinion for peace. No one knows everything, so listen to others; yielding for God's sake does you more good.
items.core_idea: Yield your opinion sometimes, for peace and God

items.plain: I often wish I had stayed quiet and kept away from people. We chatter because we hope for comfort and distraction, talking of what we love or hate, yet we seldom return to silence with a clear conscience.
items.core_idea: Much talk seldom leaves the conscience unharmed

items.plain: You can have great peace if you stop busying yourself with what others say and do. Someone absorbed in other people's affairs and neglecting their inner self cannot stay at peace; the single-hearted are blessed with peace.
items.core_idea: Mind your own inner life to find peace

items.plain: Breaking a habit is hard, and going against your own will is harder. If you can't beat small obstacles, how will you beat big ones? Resist bad habits early, before they drag you into worse.
items.core_idea: Resist bad habits early, while they are small

items.plain: Sorrows and unfair criticism are good for us sometimes. They remind us we are only passing through this world, keep us humble, and make us look harder for God's approval when people misjudge us.
items.core_idea: Adversity and unfair judgment teach humility

items.plain: No one is free of temptation while alive, because its root is inside us. One trouble passes and another comes. Running away from temptation doesn't work; we overcome it by endurance and true humility.
items.core_idea: Temptation is overcome by endurance, not flight

items.plain: Temptation starts with an unsteady mind and little trust in God; a careless person is tossed like a ship without a rudder. As fire tests iron, temptation tests a good person and shows us what we really are.
items.core_idea: Temptation reveals what we truly are

items.plain: Trials show how far a person has grown. Being devout is easy when nothing hurts; patience in hardship is real progress. Some resist big temptations but fall to small ones, which humbles them out of self-reliance.
items.core_idea: Trials prove spiritual progress

items.plain: Look to yourself and don't judge what others do. Judging others is wasted effort and leads to error and sin; examining yourself is always worthwhile. Our feelings skew our judgment, less so when we desire only God.
items.core_idea: Examine yourself instead of judging others

items.plain: Many people seek their own ends without realising it. They seem calm while things go their way, but as soon as their wishes are thwarted they are shaken and upset.
items.core_idea: Hidden self-interest shows when wishes are thwarted

items.plain: Without love no deed is worth anything, but anything done in love, however small, bears good fruit, because God looks at how much a person is able to do more than at the size of the deed.
items.core_idea: Small deeds done in love bear fruit

items.plain: Whoever loves much does much, and whoever does well does much. Doing well means serving the common good over your own. Much that looks like love is really self-will or hope of reward.
items.core_idea: Loving much and serving others is doing much

items.plain: What you can't fix in yourself or others, bear patiently until God changes it; it may be good for testing your patience. Meanwhile ask God to help you bear these things willingly.
items.core_idea: Bear patiently what you cannot change

items.plain: Be patient with other people's faults, since you have many that others must put up with. If you can't make yourself what you want, how can you remake someone else? We want others perfect but don't fix ourselves.
items.core_idea: Bear others' faults; you have your own

items.plain: We want others corrected and restricted but refuse it for ourselves, so we rarely judge our neighbour by the same standard as ourselves. And if everyone were perfect, what would we have to bear from others for God's sake?
items.core_idea: We rarely judge others by our own standard

items.plain: Each day we should renew our commitment and stir up our zeal as though it were the first day of our turning to God, asking Him to help us make a good start, since so far we have done nothing.
items.core_idea: Begin again each day as if for the first time

items.plain: If you can't examine yourself constantly, do it at least twice a day: set your intentions in the morning, and in the evening review how you did in word, deed and thought, where you may have wronged God and others.
items.core_idea: Set intentions each morning, review each evening

items.plain: Make time for meditation and think often of God's mercies. Drop idle curiosity, gossip and wandering about, and you will find enough time for reflection. The greatest saints avoided company and lived hidden with God.
items.core_idea: Cut idle talk to make time for God

items.plain: Someone said that each time he went among people he came back less of a man. Silence is easier than talking without excess. Only those who love quiet and obedience can safely speak, lead and command.
items.core_idea: Only lovers of silence speak safely

items.plain: Those most admired often fall hardest through overconfidence, so inner temptation is good for many, keeping them from pride. How clear a conscience and how much peace belong to the one who drops vain worries and hopes only in God.
items.core_idea: Temptation guards against pride; hope in God brings peace

items.plain: In solitude you find what you often lose out in the world. Kept up, solitude grows sweet; neglected, it becomes tiresome. Stay with it from the start and it becomes a dear friend and comfort.
items.core_idea: Solitude kept faithfully becomes a dear friend

items.plain: Craving for pleasure pulls you out, but after an hour you bring home only a burdened conscience and a scattered heart. A merry night makes a sad morning; bodily pleasure starts sweet and ends by eating you away.
items.core_idea: Pleasure-seeking ends in a heavy heart

items.plain: You will be miserable anywhere unless you turn to God. Why be upset when things go against your wishes? No one, not even a king or pope, escapes trouble; happiest is whoever can suffer something for God.
items.core_idea: No one escapes trouble; turn to God

items.plain: Foolish people envy the rich and powerful, but seen against heaven these things are nothing: uncertain, wearisome and never held without worry. Human happiness lies not in having plenty; a modest share is enough.
items.core_idea: A modest share is enough for happiness

items.plain: Don't lose your desire to grow spiritually; there is still time. Why delay? Start now. When you feel troubled you are nearest to blessing. You must go through fire and water, and push yourself, to overcome your faults.
items.core_idea: Start now; struggle precedes blessing

items.plain: How weak people are! Today you confess your sins, tomorrow you repeat them; you resolve and within an hour forget. So we should stay humble, knowing how quickly carelessness can lose what grace and hard work gained.
items.core_idea: Our frailty is reason for humility

items.plain: Your life here ends soon, so consider the next world. People are quickly gone and forgotten. Live each day as if you will die today; a clear conscience removes fear of death. Tomorrow is uncertain, so be ready now.
items.core_idea: Live each day as if it were your last

items.plain: The patient person purifies the soul even on earth: grieving more for the wrongdoer's malice than his own hurt, praying for and forgiving those who mistreat him, quick to apologise, quicker to pity than to anger, and mastering the flesh.
items.core_idea: Patience under injury purifies the soul

items.plain: An anxious man prayed to know whether he would persevere. God asked him what he would do if he knew, and told him to do it now. Comforted, he stopped prying into the future and sought God's will.
items.core_idea: Do now what you would do if you knew

items.plain: Fear of difficulty holds many back from growth. But those who make the most progress are the ones who bravely fight what is hardest for them; a person gains most where he most overcomes himself.
items.core_idea: Growth comes from overcoming what is hardest

items.plain: Two things most help growth in holiness: firmly pulling away from the sin you are most drawn to, and eagerly pursuing the good you most lack. Also guard hard against the faults that most annoy you in others.
items.core_idea: Fight your main weakness, pursue your main lack

items.plain: The earnest person bears whatever comes. The careless and lukewarm suffer trouble on every side, lacking inner comfort. Living without discipline invites ruin, and whoever looks for an easier discipline will always be unhappy.
items.core_idea: Earnest discipline bears all; laxity brings distress

items.plain: When a person no longer seeks comfort in any created thing, he begins to enjoy God fully and is content with whatever happens, neither overjoyed by much nor grieved by little, trusting wholly in God, in whom all things live.
items.core_idea: Seek comfort in God alone and be content

items.plain: Remember your end, and that lost time never returns. Virtue needs effort; grow cold and things go badly, be zealous and find peace. Neglect small faults and you slide into greater ones. Watch yourself, whatever others do.
items.core_idea: Lost time never returns; tend your own soul

items.plain: Don't put much trust in any mortal, however dear, or grieve much when they oppose you; people who are with you today may turn against you tomorrow. Trust God completely; He will answer for you and do what is best.
items.core_idea: People change; put your whole trust in God

items.plain: Christ was despised and abandoned by his friends, yet you complain? He had enemies, and you want everyone on your side? Without adversity patience earns no crown. To share Christ's reign, endure with Him and for Him.
items.core_idea: Christ suffered rejection; do not expect less

items.plain: The wise see things as they are, not as they seem. Someone who lives from within and values outward things little needs no special place or time for God, adapts to events, and isn't troubled by others' odd behaviour.
items.core_idea: Live from within, unmoved by outward things

items.plain: Don't worry about who is for or against you; do the duty in front of you and keep God with you. Keep a good conscience and God will defend you. Be quiet and endure, and you will see His help.
items.core_idea: Do your duty; God defends a good conscience

items.plain: Be at peace yourself first; then you can bring peace to others. A peaceful person does more good than a learned one; a restless one suspects everyone and disturbs everyone. Correct yourself before correcting your neighbour.
items.core_idea: Be at peace yourself before making peace

items.plain: You excuse yourself but not others; the reverse would be fairer. If you want others to bear with you, bear with them. Getting along with gentle people is easy; living peacefully with difficult ones is a great grace.
items.core_idea: Excuse others as readily as yourself

items.plain: Some keep peace in themselves and with others; some have no peace and give none, troubling themselves most. But our peace in this life lies in suffering humbly, not in avoiding hardship; whoever suffers best has the most peace.
items.core_idea: Peace lies in humble suffering, not avoiding hardship

items.plain: If you were pure inside, you would see everything rightly; we judge outwardly as we are inwardly. The pure in heart have the world's joy. As fire burns rust off iron, turning wholly to God makes you new.
items.core_idea: As we are inside, so we see outside

items.plain: When someone grows lukewarm, small efforts scare him and he grabs at outward comforts; when he truly starts mastering himself and following God, things that once seemed so hard count for nothing.
items.core_idea: Self-mastery makes hard things seem light

items.plain: We can't trust ourselves too little; our light is small and easily lost. We excuse our wrongs, call passion zeal, and blame small faults in others while ignoring big ones in ourselves. Self-knowledge stops harsh judgment.
items.core_idea: Knowing our faults stops us judging others

items.plain: A spiritual person cares first for his own soul and stays quiet about others. Think wholly on yourself and God, and outside things will move you little. Where are you when absent from yourself? For peace, attend to yourself.
items.core_idea: Attend to your own soul, not others' affairs

items.plain: A good conscience is a good person's glory and brings lasting joy. It can bear a great deal and stays glad in hardship, while a bad conscience is always afraid. You sleep well when your heart doesn't accuse you.
items.core_idea: A good conscience brings joy even in hardship

items.plain: Human praise is brief and brings sadness with it. Good people find their glory in conscience and their joy in God and truth. Whoever cares for neither praise nor blame has great peace of heart.
items.core_idea: Indifference to praise and blame brings peace

items.plain: A pure conscience is easily content. Praise doesn't make you holier, nor blame worse; you are what you are, and no better than God says. People see the outside and the deed, but God sees the heart and the intention.
items.core_idea: You are what you are in God's sight

items.plain: Blessed is whoever knows what it is to love Jesus above all. Love of created things is unstable and makes you fall; love of Jesus is faithful. Hold Him as your friend; He stays when everyone leaves.
items.core_idea: Jesus stays when all others leave

items.plain: Bring God a free, bare heart; only His grace unites you to Him. With grace you can do anything; without it you are weak. Don't despair then, but rest in God's will: after winter comes summer, after storm, calm.
items.core_idea: After winter summer; after storm, calm

items.plain: We grab at any comfort. For love of Christ, Saint Laurence calmly let his beloved bishop Sixtus be taken from him. Learn likewise to give up a dear friend for God, and don't resent being left; all must part.
items.core_idea: Let friends go; all must part at last

items.plain: When comfort is taken away, don't despair; wait humbly and patiently for God to return, since He can give back even more. This is familiar to those on God's way; the saints and prophets often went through it.
items.core_idea: When comfort leaves, wait patiently for its return

items.plain: I have never met anyone so devout that he didn't sometimes feel God's favour withdraw and his fervour fade. No saint was ever so enlightened that he was not tempted sooner or later.
items.core_idea: Even saints feel God withdraw sometimes

items.plain: Why look for rest when you were born to work? Prepare yourself for patience more than comfort, and for carrying the cross more than for joy.
items.core_idea: Prepare for patience more than comfort

items.plain: Be thankful for the smallest blessing and you will be worthy of greater ones. Treat the least gift as if it were the greatest, and something of little account as a special present.
items.core_idea: Gratitude for small gifts opens the way to more

items.plain: At times God seems absent, others try you, and you tire of yourself, with no relief but to bear it as God wills. You can't escape the Cross, since you take yourself everywhere; you need patience for inner peace.
items.core_idea: The Cross is everywhere; patience brings peace

items.plain: Carry your cross willingly and it will carry you to where suffering ends, though not in this life. Carry it unwillingly and it gets heavier, yet you must still carry it. Drop one and you'll find another, perhaps heavier.
items.core_idea: Carry your cross willingly and it carries you

items.plain: People travel far for a small reward but will hardly lift a foot for eternal life. They fight shamefully over a coin and toil day and night for empty things and flimsy promises.
items.core_idea: We work hard for trifles, little for eternity

items.plain: A prayer: Lord, how can I bear this hard life without Your mercy? Don't hide Your face or withhold Your comfort. Teach me to do Your will humbly, for You know me truly, and knew me before I was born.
items.core_idea: Without God's grace, life is unbearable

items.plain: Love is the greatest good: it alone makes heavy burdens light and bitter things sweet. Love of Jesus drives to great works and seeks freedom from worldly ties. Nothing is sweeter or stronger, for love is born of God.
items.core_idea: Love makes every burden light

items.plain: The one who loves flies, runs and rejoices, free, resting in God, the source of all good. Love knows no measure, feels no burden, counts no labour, and tries more than it can, succeeding where the loveless give up.
items.core_idea: Love feels no burden and attempts the impossible

items.plain: Love is quick, sincere, gentle, strong, patient, faithful and never selfish; seeking your own is falling from love. It is humble, steady and grateful to God, trusting Him even when He hides, for love cannot live without sorrow.
items.core_idea: True love is selfless and trusts through sorrow

items.plain: God speaks: fight like a good soldier, and if you sometimes fail through weakness, take up your strength more bravely, trusting in My greater grace; and beware of false confidence and pride.
items.core_idea: After failure, rise braver, trusting grace

items.plain: Those wise in their own eyes rarely accept being guided. A little wisdom with humility is better than great learning with vanity. It is better for you to have less of anything that might make you proud.
items.core_idea: Humble little wisdom beats proud great learning

items.plain: God speaks: whoever is overconfident in peace will be fearful in war. Stay humble. When fervour burns, think how it will be when the light goes; when it goes, remember it may return. Such trials help more than constant success.
items.core_idea: In good times, prepare for the light to fade

items.plain: God speaks: don't chase a desire too hard without consulting Me, or you may regret it. Not every good-seeming feeling should be followed at once. Even good desires sometimes need restraint, lest they distract you or trouble others.
items.core_idea: Even good desires sometimes need restraint

items.plain: Lord, I need patience; however I plan for peace, life brings strife. God answers: I don't want you seeking a peace free of trials; count yourself at peace when you are tested by many troubles.
items.core_idea: True peace is found amid trials

items.plain: The rich of this world will vanish like smoke, and no trace of their pleasures will remain. Even while alive they are never free of bitterness, weariness and fear.
items.core_idea: Worldly riches vanish like smoke

items.plain: An old habit will resist, but a better habit will overcome it. The body will complain again and again, but a fervent spirit will hold it in check.
items.core_idea: A better habit overcomes an old one

items.plain: If you are not led by the Spirit, there is no worse or deadlier enemy to your soul than you yourself.
items.core_idea: Without the Spirit, you are your worst enemy

items.plain: Lord, without Your hand there is no holiness, wisdom, strength or purity. Left alone we sink and perish; visited by You we rise and live. We are unstable and grow cold, but You strengthen us and rekindle us.
items.core_idea: Without God we fall; with Him we rise

items.plain: Someone humbled by Truth will not be puffed up by the whole world, nor swayed by everyone's praise if his hope is in God. Those who praise are nothing; they fade with their words, but the Lord's truth lasts forever.
items.core_idea: Praise fades; God's truth endures

items.plain: God speaks: whatever you desire, seek it humbly and in awe of God, and hand it all over to Me, saying: Lord, You know what is best; give what and when You will; I am Your servant, living for You.
items.core_idea: Lord, You know best; Your will be done

items.plain: A prayer: above everything I could want, let me rest in You and let my heart be at peace in You. You alone are the heart's true peace and rest; without You everything is hard and restless.
items.core_idea: God alone is the heart's true rest

items.plain: Want present things too much and you lose eternal ones. Use temporal things, but desire eternal ones. No earthly good can satisfy you, because you weren't made to enjoy these.
items.core_idea: Use earthly things; desire eternal ones

items.plain: All human comfort is empty and brief; the comfort that is blessed and real is felt inside and comes from the truth.
items.core_idea: Real comfort comes from within, from truth

items.plain: Lord, You care for me more than I can for myself; whoever doesn't give You his worries stands insecurely. While my will rests in You, do as You wish; it can only be good. Blessed be You, dark or light.
items.core_idea: Blessed be God in light and darkness alike

items.plain: Your suffering is small next to those who have been far more tempted and tried. Remember their pains to bear yours more easily; if yours don't seem small, impatience may be the cause. Big or small, bear them patiently.
items.core_idea: Recall others' greater sufferings to bear your own

items.plain: Someone isn't truly patient who suffers only what he thinks fair and from whom he chooses. The truly patient person accepts every hardship, from anyone, gratefully as from God, since nothing borne for God, however small, loses its reward.
items.core_idea: True patience accepts hardship from anyone

items.plain: Be ready to fight if you want to win. Without struggle there is no crown of patience; refuse to suffer and you refuse the crown. So strive bravely and endure patiently. No rest without labour, no victory without fighting.
items.core_idea: No victory without struggle, no rest without labour

items.plain: A prayer: Lord, by Your grace make possible for me what seems impossible by nature. You know how little I can bear and how quickly I am knocked down when trouble comes.
items.core_idea: Grace makes possible what nature cannot

items.plain: Lord, I confess my weakness. Small things often knock me down and make me sad. I resolve to be brave, but a little temptation throws me into crisis; just when I feel safe, a puff of wind nearly overcomes me.
items.core_idea: Small things easily overthrow our resolve

items.plain: Lord, what keeps setting me back is how easily I fall and how weakly I resist my passions. Their attacks are violent, and living in daily conflict wears me out. Hateful thoughts rush in far more easily than they leave.
items.core_idea: Bad thoughts enter easily and leave slowly

items.plain: What a life this is, where troubles never stop and everything is full of traps and enemies; when one trouble or temptation goes, another comes, and while one battle still rages, more arrive unexpectedly.
items.core_idea: In this life troubles never cease

items.plain: A prayer to Jesus: before You I have no words, and my silence speaks. How long until You come? Come, for without You no day is joyful. I feel imprisoned until Your presence refreshes and frees me.
items.core_idea: Without Jesus no day is joyful

items.plain: God speaks: Here I am; I come to you because you called Me. Your tears, your longing, your humility and sorrow of heart have drawn Me to you.
items.core_idea: God comes to the humble who call

items.plain: Someone given fewer gifts shouldn't be downcast or envy those given more, but praise God's generous goodness, the source of everything. God knows what is best for each; why one has less and another more is His to understand.
items.core_idea: Don't envy others' gifts; God knows best

items.plain: God speaks: try to do another's will rather than your own. Always choose less rather than more, seek the lowest place, and pray that God's will be done in you. Such a person enters into peace and quiet.
items.core_idea: Choose less and the lowest place for peace

items.plain: A prayer: Lord my God, don't stay far from me; hurry to help me, for many thoughts and great fears have risen against me and torment my soul. How will I get through them unharmed?
items.core_idea: A plea to God amid fears

items.plain: A prayer: Jesus, light up my heart and drive out its darkness. Calm my wandering thoughts and take away harmful temptations, so my conscience may have peace. Tell the wind and sea to be still, and there will be calm.
items.core_idea: Ask Jesus to calm the storm within

items.plain: A prayer: draw me away from the unstable comforts of created things, for none can satisfy me. Bind me to You with unbreakable love, since You alone are enough for whoever loves You; without You everything is empty toys.
items.core_idea: God alone satisfies; all else is empty

items.plain: God speaks: don't be nosy or fret over useless worries. What is that to you? Follow Me. Why should it matter what someone else is, says or does? You don't answer for others, only for yourself, so why get entangled?
items.core_idea: You answer only for yourself

items.plain: Don't trouble yourself about fame, having many friends, or being loved by people. These things bring distraction and great sorrow of heart.
items.core_idea: Fame and popularity bring distraction and sorrow

items.plain: God speaks: everyone wants peace, but not everyone cares about what true peace requires. My peace is with the humble and lowly in heart. Your peace will lie in much patience.
items.core_idea: Peace belongs to the humble and patient

items.plain: Never feeling unease or pain belongs to eternal rest, not this life. So don't think you've found true peace just because you feel no grief, have no opponent, or everything goes your way.
items.core_idea: Peace is not the absence of trouble

items.plain: Lord, the mark of a perfect person is to keep the mind on heavenly things and pass through many cares as if free of care, not out of indifference but with a free mind, clinging to nothing with excessive attachment.
items.core_idea: Pass through cares with a free mind

items.plain: God speaks: self-love harms you more than anything in the world. Things cling to you as your love clings to them; pure love leaves you captive to nothing. Don't covet what you can't have or keep what robs your freedom.
items.core_idea: Self-love harms you more than anything

items.plain: God speaks: why wear yourself out with useless sorrow and worry? Rest in My will and you lose nothing. Chase things for your own advantage or pleasure and you will never have peace; something will always be lacking.
items.core_idea: Chasing your own wishes never brings peace

items.plain: A place helps little without devotion, and peace sought outside won't last if your heart isn't grounded in God. You can change where you are, but not make yourself better that way; you'll meet what you fled, and more.
items.core_idea: Changing places won't change your heart

items.plain: God speaks: if you live inwardly, you won't give passing words more weight than they deserve. It is real wisdom to stay silent in bad times, turn inward to Me, and not be troubled by people's judgment.
items.core_idea: Keep silent and turn inward when judged

items.plain: Don't let your peace depend on what people say; good or bad, their opinion doesn't change who you are. True peace is in God. Whoever neither seeks to please people nor fears displeasing them will have great peace.
items.core_idea: Don't let your peace depend on others' words

items.plain: A prayer: Lord, I am in trouble and caught in snares. Save me from this hour, though I came to it so You may be glorified. Without You where can I go? Give me patience again, and I won't fear.
items.core_idea: In trouble, ask God for patience

items.plain: God speaks: My child, I am a stronghold when trouble comes. Come to Me when things are not well with you.
items.core_idea: Turn to God when things go wrong

items.plain: God speaks: what most blocks comfort is being slow to pray. You first try outward comforts, which help little, until you learn that I deliver those who trust Me; apart from Me there is no strong help or lasting remedy.
items.core_idea: Turn to prayer first, not last

items.plain: God speaks: stand firm and persevere; comfort will come in its time. Wait for Me; I will come and heal you. What troubles you is temptation and empty fear. Worrying about the future only adds sorrow to sorrow.
items.core_idea: Wait patiently; don't worry about tomorrow

items.plain: God speaks: don't let your heart be troubled or afraid; trust My mercy. When you feel far from Me, I am often nearest. When all seems lost, gain is often close. Don't judge by present feelings or give up hope.
items.core_idea: When all seems lost, God is often near

items.plain: God speaks: don't think yourself abandoned when I send trouble or take away a comfort you love; this is the way to heaven. It is better for you to be tested by hardship than to get everything you want.
items.core_idea: Hardship is not abandonment by God

items.plain: What is more peaceful than a single-minded heart, and who is freer than the one who wants nothing on earth?
items.core_idea: Wanting nothing on earth brings freedom

items.plain: We ask what someone has achieved, rich, strong, clever, talented, but rarely how humble, patient, gentle or devout they are. Human nature looks at the outside and often misjudges; grace looks to the heart and trusts God.
items.core_idea: We judge by achievements; grace looks at the heart

items.plain: God speaks: you can't be fully free without denying yourself. The rich, the selfish and the restless are slaves, and what isn't from God will perish. Give up everything and you find everything; give up craving and you find rest.
items.core_idea: Give up craving and you will find rest

items.plain: God speaks: don't be put off or discouraged when you hear what the perfect way demands. Let it spur you to higher aims, or at least to long for that desire.
items.core_idea: High ideals should inspire, not discourage

items.plain: God speaks: don't trust your feelings; they change quickly, joyful then sad, calm then anxious, devout then careless. The wise rise above these moods, keeping their aim fixed on God, so they stay steady through all the world's changes.
items.core_idea: Moods change; keep your aim fixed on God

items.plain: My God, my all! For those who understand, those words are enough. When You are present everything is pleasant; when You are absent everything is tiresome. You give the heart rest, deep peace and festive joy.
items.core_idea: With God everything is pleasant

items.plain: If you look for rest in this life, how will you reach eternal rest? Aim not for much rest but for much patience. Seek true peace not on earth, in people or in things, but in God alone.
items.core_idea: Seek patience, not rest; peace in God alone

items.plain: God speaks: do you expect spiritual comfort whenever you want? My saints had grief and desolation instead, yet bore it patiently and trusted God. Don't demand at once what others won through tears. Wait, be strong; I am with you.
items.core_idea: Saints endured desolation; wait for the Lord

items.plain: God speaks: anchor your soul in God and don't fear people's judgment when your conscience says you are innocent. Such suffering is good for a humble heart. People's opinions vary, so trust them little; you can't please everyone anyway.
items.core_idea: Anchor in God; you cannot please everyone

items.plain: Why fear a mortal who is here today and gone tomorrow? Fear God and you won't cower before people's threats. What can anyone do to you by word or deed? He harms himself more, and won't escape God's judgment.
items.core_idea: Fear God, not mortal people

items.plain: God speaks: lose yourself and you will find Me. Stand still, without choosing or thinking of yourself, and you will always gain. More grace comes the moment you give yourself up, as long as you don't take yourself back.
items.core_idea: Lose yourself and you will find God

items.plain: God speaks: give yourself up and you will have great inner peace. Give all for all, ask nothing back, rest simply in Me. Let go of self and follow Jesus; then vain fancies, needless worries and excessive fear will vanish.
items.core_idea: Surrender yourself and find inner peace

items.plain: A prayer: Lord, I gladly hand everything over to You, since my planning helps little. If only I didn't dwell so much on the future, but gave myself wholly to Your will at once.
items.core_idea: Hand plans to God; stop dwelling on the future

items.plain: God speaks: people often chase something hard, then lose interest once they have it, because desires don't last but jump from one thing to the next. So resisting yourself even in small things is no small matter.
items.core_idea: Desires fade once fulfilled

items.plain: Vanity is a terrible plague, the greatest of vanities, because it pulls us from true glory and robs us of God's grace. While a person pleases himself he displeases God; while he craves praise, he loses real virtue.
items.core_idea: Craving praise robs us of true virtue

items.plain: God speaks: don't let it concern you if others are honoured and you are looked down on. Lift your heart to Me in heaven, and people's contempt on earth won't make you sad.
items.core_idea: Lift your heart above others' contempt

items.plain: God speaks: if your peace rests on a person you admire, you'll be unstable. Rest in lasting Truth and a friend's leaving or death won't crush you. Love friends in and for God; without Him friendship has no lasting strength.
items.core_idea: Ground friendship in God, not in the friend

items.plain: Let many things pass unheard and think about what brings you peace. Better to look away from what displeases you and let others keep their opinions than to argue. If you stand well with God, losing an argument is easy.
items.core_idea: Let others keep their opinions; avoid strife

items.plain: Lord, what have we come to? We mourn worldly losses and rush after small gains, yet forget spiritual losses. We tend what matters little and neglect what is essential, because we slide toward outward things and settle there.
items.core_idea: We mourn small losses and forget spiritual ones

items.plain: Lord, help me in trouble, for human help is useless. I often found no loyalty where I expected it, and found it where I didn't. Hope in people is vain; salvation is in You. We are weak and easily deceived.
items.core_idea: Human help fails; hope rests in God

items.plain: A friend who stays loyal through all your troubles is rare. You alone, Lord, are faithful in everything, and there is no one like You.
items.core_idea: Loyal friends are rare; God is faithful

items.plain: Someone says, 'Keep this secret,' then can't keep it himself and betrays us both. Lord, protect me from such reckless gossips and keep me from doing the same. What I wouldn't want done to me, I must not do.
items.core_idea: Don't do what you would not want done

items.plain: How good and peaceful it is not to talk about others, not to believe or spread every rumour, to open up to few, to keep God as your heart's witness, and not be blown about by every wind of words.
items.core_idea: Silence about others brings peace

items.plain: God speaks: stand firm and trust Me. What are words but words? They fly through the air but bruise no stone. If you are guilty, think how to improve; if your conscience is clear, bear it gladly for God.
items.core_idea: Words fly by but bruise no stone

items.plain: God speaks: listen to My word and you won't care about ten thousand human words. Even if the worst malice said everything against you, what harm if you let it go like dust? Could it touch one hair?
items.core_idea: Malicious words cannot truly harm you

items.plain: No evil comes to the just, whatever God sends them. Even if falsely accused, they care little; and if others clear their name, they don't celebrate too much.
items.core_idea: The just stay steady when accused or cleared

items.plain: God speaks: don't let your work for Me break you or troubles cast you down; let My promise comfort you. I can reward you beyond measure. You won't labour or grieve forever; wait a little and your troubles will end.
items.core_idea: Troubles are brief; wait a little longer

items.plain: God speaks: do whatever you do wholeheartedly; work faithfully in My vineyard and I will be your reward. Write, read, sing, weep, keep silent, pray, bear hardship bravely; eternal life is worth all these struggles and more.
items.core_idea: Work wholeheartedly; eternal life is worth it

items.plain: The days of this life are few and hard, full of sorrow: people are stained by sin, trapped by passions, bound by fears, worn by cares and labour, weighed down by temptation, weakened by pleasure, tormented by poverty.
items.core_idea: Life's days are few and full of burdens

items.plain: Lord, I long to know You closely but can't; worldly things and untamed passions drag me down. My mind wants to rise above everything, my body pulls me under, so I fight myself and become a burden to myself.
items.core_idea: Spirit rises, flesh pulls down; I fight myself

items.plain: Often I'm not really where my body stands or sits, but wherever my thoughts carry me. Where my thought is, there I am, and my thought is usually where what I love is, drawn by delight or habit.
items.core_idea: You are where your thoughts are

items.plain: As Christ said, where your treasure is, your heart will be. If I love heaven, I think of heavenly things; if I love the world, its pleasures and troubles move me. Whatever I love fills my talk and my thoughts.
items.core_idea: Where your treasure is, your heart is

items.plain: God speaks: a fire often burns, but its flame rises with smoke. Some people's longing for heaven burns, yet bodily desire still clings to it, so their prayer isn't purely for God. Yours is often like that, tainted by self-seeking.
items.core_idea: Even earnest devotion carries some self-seeking

items.plain: God speaks: you will often have to do what you don't want and leave undone what you do. Others will succeed, be heard, get what they ask and be praised; you won't, and you'll be thought useless.
items.core_idea: Others will be favoured while you are passed over

items.plain: God speaks: hardly anything requires more self-denial than facing what goes against your will, especially orders that seem pointless. Because you are under authority and can't resist, it feels hard to follow another's direction and give up your own opinion.
items.core_idea: Obeying against your own opinion is hard

items.plain: A prayer: I long for the peace You give Your children. If You give peace and joy, my soul will sing Your praise. But when You withdraw, as You often do, I falter and beat my breast.
items.core_idea: When God withdraws, peace and joy fade

items.plain: Lord, it was good for me to be in trouble, so I could learn Your ways and drop my pride. It helped me to be put to shame, so I would look to You for comfort rather than to people.
items.core_idea: Trouble and shame turn us toward God

items.plain: A prayer: Lord, let me know what should be known, love what should be loved, and value what You value. Don't let me judge by appearances or ignorant talk, but discern truly between visible and spiritual things.
items.core_idea: Grant me to judge as God judges

items.plain: Our senses often misjudge, and worldly people love only what they see. Is anyone better because people think him great? The vain and blind praise each other foolishly. As Saint Francis said, you are what you are in God's eyes.
items.core_idea: You are what you are in God's eyes

items.plain: God speaks: you can't always stay in fervent desire for virtue or high contemplation; your fallen nature means you must sometimes come down to lower things. While you have a mortal body, you will feel weariness and heaviness of heart.
items.core_idea: In a mortal body, weariness is unavoidable

items.plain: What does God ask of a guilty sinner but sorrow and humility? From true sorrow and humility come hope of pardon, a reconciled conscience and recovered grace, and God and the repentant soul hurry to meet each other.
items.core_idea: Humble sorrow brings God and sinner together

items.plain: God speaks: if you fully conquer yourself, you'll easily master everything else. The perfect victory is over yourself. Whoever keeps his desires obedient to reason, and his reason obedient to Me, truly rules himself and the world.
items.core_idea: The perfect victory is over oneself

items.plain: Nature works for its own advantage and looks for what it can gain from others; Grace looks not at what is useful to itself but at what will benefit many.
items.core_idea: Nature seeks self; grace seeks the good of many

items.plain: Nature cares for passing things, delights in money, is saddened by loss and stung by any hurtful word. Grace reaches for eternal things, isn't upset by losses or embittered by harsh words, because its treasure and joy are in heaven.
items.core_idea: Grace is unshaken by loss and harsh words

items.plain: Nature is greedy, likes receiving more than giving, and loves what is private to itself; Grace is kind and generous, avoids selfishness, is content with little, and believes it is more blessed to give than to receive.
items.core_idea: Grace finds more blessing in giving

items.plain: So I want to do good but can't do it. I plan good things, but without grace I give up at the slightest resistance. I see clearly what I should do, yet my corruption keeps me from rising to it.
items.core_idea: I see the good but fail to do it

items.plain: God speaks: as far as you go out of yourself, so far can you enter into Me. Wanting nothing outward brings inner peace; letting go of self unites you with God. Learn full self-denial, living in My will without complaint.
items.core_idea: Leave yourself to enter into God

items.plain: Truly the life of a devoted servant is a cross, but it leads to paradise. I have started; I may not turn back or give it up.
items.core_idea: The cross leads to paradise; don't turn back

items.plain: God speaks: patience and humility in hardship please Me more than comfort in good times. Why does a small criticism upset you? Let it pass; it won't be the last. You give good advice until trouble knocks at your door.
items.core_idea: Patience in hardship outweighs comfort in ease

items.plain: God speaks: if you can't bear it joyfully, at least bear it patiently. Even if angry, hold back hasty words that could hurt others. The storm will soon calm and grace will sweeten your grief. Trust and call on Me.
items.core_idea: Bear patiently if not joyfully; the storm will pass
